scenarios.title: Full trip plan (Jaipur)
scenarios.purpose: End-to-end planning: weather, guide and budget tools, then JSON itinerary via the output parser.

turns.user: Plan a 3-day trip to Jaipur for 2 people starting 21 September 2026. We love forts and local food. Our budget is about ₹30,000 in total and we are coming from Delhi.
turns.answer:
### Overview
A royal 3-day getaway from Delhi to the Pink City of Jaipur for 2 people, focused on historic forts and delectable Rajasthani cuisine, staying comfortably within your ₹30,000 budget.

### Weather
The live forecast for Jaipur from September 21 to September 23, 2026, indicates **clear skies and warm weather** (highs around 32°C to 33°C, lows around 23°C to 24°C). It will be sunny during the day, so bring sunscreen and hats, but the evenings will be pleasant for outdoor exploring.

### Day-by-Day Plan

#### Day 1: Royal Palaces & Sunset Views
*   **Morning**: Take the early morning Ajmer Shatabdi Express from Delhi (approx. 6:10 AM – 10:40 AM). Check into a charming mid-range heritage hotel (such as *Hotel Pearl Palace* or *Umaid Bhawan*).
*   **Afternoon**: Head into the Old City for a traditional Rajasthani lunch at the iconic **LMB (Laxmi Mishthan Bhandar)**. Afterward, visit the stunning **Hawa Mahal** (Palace of Winds) and the adjacent **City Palace** to marvel at the royal courtyards and museum collections.
*   **Evening**: Catch an auto-rickshaw or taxi up to **Nahargarh Fort** (Tiger Fort) for a spectacular sunset view over the Pink City. Enjoy dinner at *Peacock Rooftop Restaurant* or at the fort's terrace restaurant.

#### Day 2: Grand Forts & Cultural Feast
*   **Morning**: Beat the heat and head north early (around 8:30 AM) to the magnificent **Amber Fort** (Indian entry is ₹100). Wander through the mirror-adorned *Sheesh Mahal* (Glass Palace). Skip the elephant rides due to animal welfare concerns and enjoy the walk or take a jeep. Continue uphill to **Jaigarh Fort** to view *Jaivana*, once the world's largest cannon on wheels.
*   **Afternoon**: Stop by the picturesque **Jal Mahal** (Water Palace) for photos on your way back. For a late lunch, indulge in the legendary, spicy *Pyaz Kachoris* at **Rawat Mishthan Bhandar** and grab a thick, sweet clay-pot lassi at the famous **Lassiwala** on MI Road.
*   **Evening**: Travel to **Chokhi Dhani**, an ethnic Rajasthani village resort. Experience lively folk dances, puppet shows, and camel rides before enjoying an unlimited, authentic *Dal Baati Churma* feast served traditionally on leaf platters.

#### Day 3: Science, Souvenirs & Sweet Treats
*   **Morning**: Visit **Jantar Mantar**, a fascinating UNESCO World Heritage site featuring giant, precise astronomical stone instruments and the world's largest stone sundial.
*   **Afternoon**: Spend your final hours shopping for local handicrafts, block-print textiles, and jewelry at the vibrant **Johari Bazaar** and **Bapu Bazaar**. Stop by *Gangaur Sweets* for a quick bite and pack some fresh *Ghevar* (sweet) to take back to Delhi.
*   **Evening**: Board the return Shatabdi or Double Decker train back to Delhi, arriving by night.

### Budget Table (Estimates for 2 People)

| Item | Details | Cost (INR) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Intercity Travel** | Return Shatabdi AC Chair Car from Delhi | ₹3,000 |
| **Accommodation** | 2 Nights in a boutique heritage hotel / haveli | ₹8,000 |
| **Local Transport** | Dedicated auto-rickshaws or cabs for 3 days | ₹3,600 |
| **Food & Drinks** | Meals, street food, and lassis (excluding Chokhi Dhani) | ₹5,400 |
| **Activities & Entry**| Fort entries & the Chokhi Dhani buffet package | ₹4,000 |
| **Contingency** | 10% safety margin | ₹2,400 |
| **Total Estimated Cost** | | **₹26,400** |

### Practical Tips
*   **Composite Tickets**: Purchase the Jaipur Composite Ticket at your first monument. It covers Amber Fort, Nahargarh, Hawa Mahal, Jantar Mantar, and Albert Hall, saving you money and booking time.
*   **Local Bargaining**: When hiring auto-rickshaws for the day, agree on an "all-inclusive" price that covers parking, petrol, and waiting times to avoid hidden charges.
*   **Holidays**: Verified public holiday data for India could not be retrieved for these dates.

### Sources & Caveats
*   **Sources**: Weather from Open-Meteo Forecast API (live forecast); travel guide details from Wikivoyage (Amber Fort pricing & dining recommendations).
*   **Caveats**: Monument entry prices, train fares, and hotel tariffs are realistic estimates and may vary slightly depending on booking time and tourist season. Public holiday data could not be verified.

tools.name: get_destination_guide
tools.output:
{"ok": true, "page": "Jaipur", "section": "Get around", "source": "Wikivoyage (MediaWiki API)", "text": "By RTDC bus:
It is the best and cheaper way to visit the Jaipur Local Sights by RTDC (Rajasthan Tourism Dept. Corp.) There will be one guide with each bus to give you brief info about all sights. The full day tour, as of 2019, costs ₹600.

By metro:
The Jaipur Metro provides a fast, reliable and inexpensive way to get around the city. The Pink Line  Metro  runs from Mansarovar to Badi Chaupar station, which is in the centre of the walled town (a.k.a the Pink City). Fares range between ₹5 and ₹25.

By autorickshaw:
Autorickshaws (tuk-tuks) are probably the best way to reach places in the outskirts of Jaipur such as Amber Fort or Galtaji, where getting a taxi or Uber/Ola to go back to the city may be tricky. They are generally more expensive than Uber/Ola, but they are readily available and don't require waiting time.
Hiring an autorickshaw for a whole day to go to Amber Fort, Tiger Fort, Jal Mahal, and other areas costs anywhere between ₹450 to ₹550 (as of 2018). A common scam is drivers asking for extra money throughout the day for parking fees, petrol, and other things along the way. Always agree on an ‘all-in’ price that includes their time, petrol, lunch, and parking fees. It's not uncommon for people to agree to ₹500 and pay close to ₹1000 with all of the surprise fees. Lastly, make sure you and the driver agree that they will take you to the site and not close to it ‘just for photographs’.
Prepaid autos are available at the Jaipur railway station and the Sindhi Camp bus stand, although prices are a little inflated and often the same as you get with minimal bargaining.
At a certain point, the rates were revised to ₹350-400. The autorickshaw wallas will tell you to take the slip from the police booths. You can also go directly without the slip, but don't forget to bargain over the price in that case; it could be much cheaper. It'll be best if you start your sightseeing by 10:00 as some of the major spots close by 16:30 and each spot takes a lot of time, especially the forts.
Some autorickshaw drivers will try to trick you into paying more than the agreed amount after the trip is over, but you should stick to the original amount decided. Police in Jaipur are very friendly, so in case you feel the autorickshaw driver is trying to misguide you or force you to hand over extra money, just refer the dispute to the police officers at various spots. …", "truncated": true, "url": "https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Jaipur", "license": "Wikivoyage, CC BY-SA 4.0"}

turns.user: Nice. What should I see there? Also estimate a budget for one person in INR.
turns.answer:
### Udaipur: The Romantic City of Lakes
Known for its striking palaces, calm lakes, and lush green hills, Udaipur is the perfect destination for a brief, scenic escape.

### Weather Summary (23–24 September 2026)
* **Conditions:** Clear to mainly clear skies with no expected rainfall.
* **Temperatures:** Highs around 31°C and lows near 22°C. 
* *(Source: Live forecast via Open-Meteo).*

---

### 2-Day Itinerary

#### **Day 1: Imperial Palaces & Lakeside Sunsets (23 September)**
* **Morning:** Arrive in Udaipur and check into your accommodation. Head straight to the grand **City Palace**, a stunning granite and marble complex overlooking Lake Pichola. Wander its courtyards, mirror-work balconies, and the elevated garden of *Amar Vilas*.
* **Afternoon:** Take a scenic boat ride from the palace grounds across **Lake Pichola** to visit the island palace of **Jag Mandir**.
* **Evening:** Walk over to **Ambrai Ghat** or **Bagore-ki-Haveli** to enjoy a magical sunset view over the lake and watch the palaces light up. 

#### **Day 2: Royal Gardens & Panoramic Hills (24 September)**
* **Morning:** Visit **Saheliyon-ki-Bari** (Garden of the Maidens), famous for its lush lawns, lotus pools, and beautifully carved marble fountains.
* **Afternoon:** Take a cab up to the **Monsoon Palace (Sajjangarh)** perched high on a hill, offering spectacular panoramic views of Udaipur's lakes and the surrounding Aravalli range.
* **Evening:** Do some souvenir shopping at **Hathi Pol Bazaar** (famous for Rajasthani miniature paintings and handicrafts) before heading back to the station/airport for your departure.

---

### Estimated Budget (1 Person, 1 Night)

All prices are realistic estimates calculated in INR:

| Budget Item | Estimated Cost (INR) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Intercity Travel** (Return train/flight) | ₹5,000 |
| **Accommodation** (1 Night, mid-range) | ₹3,000 |
| **Food & Drink** (₹1,000/day for 2 days) | ₹2,000 |
| **Local Transport** (Cabs/auto-rickshaws, ₹1,000/day) | ₹2,000 |
| **Activities & Entry Tickets** (Palace entry, boat ride, Sajjangarh) | ₹1,500 |
| **Contingency** (10% safety margin) | ₹1,350 |
| **Total Estimated Budget** | **₹14,850** |

---

### Practical Tips
* **Lakes are Full:** Because September marks the end of the monsoon season, the lakes will be full and the surrounding hills will be beautifully green and scenic.
* **Advance Bookings:** If you plan on taking the Lake Pichola boat ride at sunset, try to purchase your ticket a bit earlier in the afternoon as sunset slots fill up quickly.

***

*Sources & caveats: Weather data sourced from Open-Meteo live forecast. Destination details from Wikivoyage. The budget is a planning estimate; actual travel costs may vary depending on your starting city and choice of lodging.*

A complex of small and big palaces, museums and gardens encompassing a rich blend of Rajasthani, Mughal, Medieval, European and Chinese architecture established in 1559 by Maharana Udai Mirza Singh. turns.user: Plan 3 days in Manali from 16 November 2026 to 18 November 2026. I like mountains and easy hikes.
turns.answer:
Experience crisp Himalayan air, ancient cedar forests, and scenic valley trails with this 3-day itinerary for Manali, Himachal Pradesh, from **16 November 2026 to 18 November 2026**.

### Weather & Season
* **Forecast Note:** Mid-November falls outside the 16-day live forecast window. Based on historical data observed on these exact dates last year, expect crisp, clear days with maximum temperatures around 18°C and chilly nights dropping near or slightly below freezing (approx. -0.2°C average low). Pack warm layers, gloves, and a good jacket!

---

### Day-by-Day Itinerary

#### Day 1: Arrival & Cedar Forest Exploration (16 Nov)
* **Morning:** Arrive in Manali, check into your hotel, and settle in. 
* **Afternoon:** Head to **Old Manali** and visit the historic **Hidimba Temple**, peacefully tucked inside a dense Dhungri cedar forest. Enjoy an easy, scenic stroll beneath the towering trees.
* **Evening:** Wander through the bohemian streets of Old Manali, browse local crafts, and enjoy dinner at a cozy mountain café.

#### Day 2: Jogini Waterfall Easy Hike (17 Nov)
* **Morning:** Take a short drive to Vashisht village. Begin your gentle hike toward **Jogini Waterfall**, winding through pine forests, apple orchards, and small traditional pahari settlements with stunning valley views.
* **Afternoon:** Reach the waterfall, relax by the cascading streams, and enjoy packed snacks or a warm cup of tea at a local stall near the falls. Hike back down to Vashisht.
* **Evening:** Soothe your muscles in the natural hot sulphur springs at Vashisht Temple, followed by a relaxed dinner back in central Manali.

#### Day 3: Solang Valley & Departure (18 Nov)
* **Morning:** Take a short trip to **Solang Valley** for panoramic mountain views. If you enjoy gentle exploration, take the cable car or enjoy short ridge walks surrounded by snow-dusted peaks.
* **Afternoon:** Grab lunch with a view of the Beas River, pick up some local Kullu shawls or honey, and prepare for your onward journey home.

---

### Estimated Trip Budget (For 2 Travellers, 2 Nights)

| Expense Item | Total (INR) |
| :--- | --- |
| Accommodation (2 nights @ ₹3,500/night) | ₹7,000 |
| Intercity Travel (Return bus/cabs) | ₹5,000 |
| Food & Drinks (₹1,200 per person/day) | ₹7,200 |
| Local Transport (Cabs/autos for sightseeing) | ₹4,500 |
| Activities & Entry Fees (Temple/cable car/guide) | ₹3,000 |
| **Subtotal** | **₹26,700** |
| Contingency (10%) | ₹2,670 |
| **Total Estimated Budget** | **₹29,370** |
*(Approx. ₹14,685 per person)*

---

### Practical Tips
* **Altitude & Layering:** At ~2,050 meters, temperatures drop sharply after sunset. Layering (thermal innerwear, fleece, and a windproof jacket) is essential.
* **Daylight:** Days are shorter in November; aim to start your hikes by 9:30 AM to make the most of the sunlight.

### Sources & Cautions
* **Services Used:** Open-Meteo (Geocoding & Historical Weather Proxy), Wikivoyage (Manali Guide), and TripMate budget estimation tools.
* **Caveat:** Weather figures are based on last year's observed seasonal data for mid-November and serve as a guide rather than a live forecast.

Verified public holiday data for India is unavailable for October 2026 through the official holiday service. 

However, looking at typical seasonal calendars for Agra and northern India in October:
* **Major Festivals:** **Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti** falls on **October 2** (a national public holiday). Depending on the lunar calendar, major Hindu festivals like **Dussehra (Vijayadashami)** and **Sharad Purnima** often fall in October, bringing high numbers of domestic tourists. In 2026, Dussehra falls around late September to early October.
* **Crowd Management in Agra:** October marks the beginning of the peak tourist season in Agra as the monsoon ends and cooler weather arrives. To avoid the heaviest crowds at the Taj Mahal and Agra Fort:
  * Visit on weekdays (Tuesday through Thursday are generally quieter than Fridays—when the Taj Mahal is closed—and weekends).
  * Arrive for sunrise opening to experience the monuments before tour buses and large crowds pour in.

*Sources & caveats:* The public holiday tool returned no data (`error: no_data`), so festival details are based on general historical timing rather than verified 2026 holiday schedule queries. Geocoding confirmed Agra, Uttar Pradesh, India.
